objective: Observe owned X11 window-manager recovery and candidate continuity independently of visible placement, preserving original failures and platform gates.
decisions: Reuse the existing optional X11 runner, lab, marker renderer and pixel oracle; keep recovery outside the unchanged reveal interval.
Require pidfd-confirmed old-process exit before one replacement, then bind its supporting resource through the X server to its actual PID.
Treat an XID as reusable, not a process lifetime; preserve the failed optional-property and full-XID equality assumptions.
Keep manager recovery, candidate progress, capture coverage, wallpaper and visible recovery as distinct results.

checks.name: Three color-profile owned manager restarts with verified native identity and pixel evidence
Three delayed-image-profile owned manager restarts with unchanged wallpaper
Visible recovery of the current window-stacking candidates
Existing native input/image regression across three candidates
Nine recovery evidence checks per restart profile and fifteen input evidence checks
Three original failed observer attempts retained with source archives
Specification schemas/fixtures, generated indexes, integrity and tooling checks
Product renderer/collector continuity and other native platform qualification

open_questions: Conforming native composition still needs a strategy that preserves wallpaper and icon pixels while displaying the scene.
Icon-manager/compositor crashes, full renderer/controller/collector recovery and post-recovery input remain unqualified.
Windows needs an admitted synthetic interactive display; existing guest scope and Mac laboratory availability remain open.
next_step: Investigate conforming composition using separate reveal, icon, wallpaper and recovery evidence; continue independent native tracks where their laboratories are admitted.
limitations: The full campaign and W-02/W-05/W-25 remain incomplete; no desktop profile or product release is qualified.
Only owned synthetic Xvfb content and exact retained Openbox children were controlled; user desktop, shell, wallpaper and VMs were untouched.
The private Windows window-station finding is documentation-based, not an executed capture experiment.
C++ artifacts and build profiles did not change; prior CTest and smoke records retain their original checkpoint identities.
